meta.title: The mechanical movement: understand it and explain it
meta.description: In twenty minutes, understand how a mechanical watch works and learn to explain it simply to your clients, objections included.
obj.functions: Explain the role of the five functions of a mechanical movement, from energy to display.
obj.care: Link a situation reported by a client to how their watch works, and give them the right advice.
obj.explain: Answer a client's objection with the listen, show, connect method.
s-principe.title: The principle
welcome.title: A machine without a battery
welcome.hook.heading: “How does it work without a battery?”
welcome.hook.body:
It is the question your clients ask most often when they turn a mechanical watch over. The answer fits in one sentence: **a tiny spring-driven motor, regulated by a balance that beats several times a second**. No battery, no electronics: only mechanics.

In this module, you will discover what happens inside, link what your clients experience to how their watch works, and practise explaining it without jargon.
welcome.goals.heading: By the end of this module, you will be able to:
s-fonctions.title: The five functions
five-functions.title: From energy to display
five-functions.map.intro: Every mechanical watch performs five functions, always in the same order. Select each marker to discover the part that does the job; the dotted line follows the path of the energy.
five-functions.map.alt: Diagram of a mechanical movement seen from the back: a large barrel with its coiled spring on the left, a chain of gear wheels in the middle, the escape wheel and pallet fork on the right, the balance with its blue hairspring at the top right, and a small dial at the bottom. A copper dotted line links the barrel to the balance through the wheels.
fn.barrel.title: 1. Energy: the barrel
fn.barrel.body: A long spring, the **mainspring**, is coiled inside a toothed drum: the barrel. Winding the watch means tensioning this spring. As it unwinds, it turns the barrel, which drives the whole movement. On an automatic watch, an oscillating weight (the rotor) winds it with the movements of the wrist.
fn.train.title: 2. Transmission: the gear train
fn.train.body: A series of gear wheels carries the energy from the barrel to the escapement. Each one turns at a precise speed: the centre wheel makes one turn an hour, the seconds wheel one turn a minute. Their arbors turn in **synthetic rubies**, which reduce friction and wear.
fn.escapement.title: 3. Distribution: the escapement
fn.escapement.body: The energy must not run out all at once. The escape wheel is locked then released, tooth by tooth, by a **pallet fork** that rocks from side to side. With each rock, the pallet fork gives the balance a small impulse. This mechanism produces the tick-tock.
fn.balance.title: 4. Regulation: the balance and hairspring
fn.balance.body: This is **the heart of the watch**. The balance is a ring that swings one way then the other, brought back by a very fine spring, the hairspring. Its oscillations always last the same time: it is what measures time.
fn.display.title: 5. Display: the hands
fn.display.body: The hands turn this regular motion into hours, minutes and seconds. A small train of wheels, the **motion works**, divides the speed of the minute hand by twelve to drive the hour hand. Extra functions, such as the date or the chronograph, are called complications.
energy-path.heading: Example: follow the energy, as you would explain it
energy-path.body:
Imagine you are showing a client the transparent caseback of a watch. Here is how to walk them through it, step by step.

**1. “It all starts with the spring.”** The crown (or the rotor, on an automatic) winds the mainspring in the barrel. *What the client can see: the rotor turning when you tilt the watch.*

**2. “The spring turns the wheels.”** As it unwinds, it drives the gear train. *Show: the golden wheels and their rubies.*

**3. “The energy is released drop by drop.”** The escapement holds back the gear train and releases it tooth by tooth. *Let them hear: the tick-tock, with the watch close to their ear.*

**4. “The balance sets the beat.”** It swings at a constant rate: it is the heart of the watch. *Show: the ring moving back and forth without stopping.*

**5. “And the hands display the time.”** *The link the client makes on their own: what they have just seen moving is what drives their hands.*
heart.title: The heart of the watch
heart.intro: The balance and hairspring prompt your clients' most technical questions. Here are three answers to keep in mind.
heart.frequency.title: Frequency
heart.frequency.body:
It is expressed in vibrations per hour or in hertz. **28,800 vibrations per hour = 4 hertz = 8 vibrations per second**: the most common frequency. There are also 21,600 (3 hertz) and 36,000 (5 hertz).

A higher frequency keeps the rate steadier against disturbances, but it needs more energy and wears the parts more: it is not simply “better”.
heart.seconds.title: The sweeping seconds hand
heart.seconds.body: On a mechanical watch, the seconds hand seems to sweep. In fact, it moves in **small steps, at the rhythm of the balance**: 8 per second at 4 hertz. On a quartz watch it jumps once a second. It is a detail you can show the client, watch in hand.
heart.precision.title: Precision
heart.precision.body:
A mechanical watch gains or loses **a few seconds a day**. The title of **chronometer** is awarded after official tests lasting several days: the average daily rate must stay between −4 and +6 seconds. An ordinary quartz watch drifts by about 15 seconds a month.

The rate of a mechanical watch also varies with its position, temperature, magnetism and how wound the spring is.
practice-order.prompt: Practise: put the five functions in the order the energy follows, from the spring to the hands.
practice-order.energy.fb: The starting point: the mainspring, wound in the barrel, stores the energy.
practice-order.transmission.fb: As it unwinds, the spring turns the series of wheels that carries the energy.
practice-order.distribution.fb: At the end of the gear train, the escapement releases the energy tooth by tooth.
practice-order.regulation.fb: The escapement's impulses keep the balance swinging, and the balance sets the beat.
practice-order.display.fb: Finally, the hands turn this rhythm into hours, minutes and seconds.
s-quotidien.title: Day to day
daily-life.title: Living with a mechanical watch
daily.intro: Behind every client question, there is a part of the movement. Open each situation to know what to answer.
daily.winding.title: “How long does it run if I don't wear it?”
daily.winding.body: For its **power reserve**: often 38 to 50 hours for a common movement, sometimes more than 70 hours. Then it stops: just wind it and set the time again. A hand-wound watch is ideally wound every morning at the same time; an automatic worn every day winds itself.
daily.magnetism.title: “My watch has been gaining a lot lately.”
daily.magnetism.body: Think of **magnetism**. A magnetised hairspring sticks slightly to itself, and the watch can gain several tens of seconds a day. The culprits: speakers, magnetic bag clasps, tablets. A watchmaker demagnetises it in a few minutes.
daily.shocks.title: “Can I play sport with it?”
daily.shocks.body: A **shock-protection system** protects the balance's delicate pivots. It absorbs everyday knocks, but not a fall onto a hard floor. For high-impact activities, it is better to take it off.
daily.water.title: “Can I swim with it?”
daily.water.body: It depends on its water resistance, and water resistance depends on **gaskets that age**. It is checked at each service. Before any contact with water, the crown must be pushed in, or screwed down if it is a screw-down crown.
daily.service.title: “Does it need servicing?”
daily.service.body: Yes: the oils in the movement age, even when nothing is wrong. A **full service every five to seven years** is generally recommended, depending on the brand and use: dismantling, cleaning, lubrication, gasket replacement and regulation.
misconceptions.title: Common misconceptions
misconceptions.intro: You will often hear these four misconceptions. Knowing the answer lets you reassure without bluntly contradicting.
myth.auto.title: “It winds itself even when it's off the wrist”
myth.auto.body: No. An automatic winds itself **when it is worn**: the movement of the wrist turns the rotor. Left on a table, it stops at the end of its power reserve.
myth.stopped.title: “It stopped, so it's broken”
myth.stopped.body:
Most of the time, its spring has simply **run down**: just wear it or wind it, then set the time.

Practical tip: on many movements, it is best not to change the date when the watch shows between 9 p.m. and 3 a.m., because the date mechanism is then engaged.
myth.jewels.title: “More jewels, better watch”
myth.jewels.body: No. The rubies act as bearings against friction, and their number depends mainly on **how the movement is built and what it does**. A high number is not, in itself, a sign of quality.
myth.magnets.title: “Magnetism is a thing of the past”
myth.magnets.body: On the contrary: sources of magnets have **multiplied** in our daily lives (phones, speakers, clasps, tablets). It is even one of the most frequent causes of a watch gaining.
practice-chrono.prompt: Practise: a client reads “chronometer” on a dial and asks you what it means. What do you say?
practice-chrono.certified: The movement passed official precision tests: on average between −4 and +6 seconds a day.
practice-chrono.certified.fb: The title of chronometer certifies the movement's precision, measured over several days of official tests.
practice-chrono.stopwatch: The watch has a stopwatch function.
practice-chrono.stopwatch.fb: That function is called a chronograph: it is a complication, unrelated to the chronometer title. The two are very often confused.
practice-chrono.perfect: The watch is guaranteed accurate to the second.
practice-chrono.perfect.fb: Even certified, a mechanical watch gains or loses a few seconds a day: the title sets a tolerance, not perfection.
s-expliquer.title: Explaining it to the client
method.title: Listen, show, connect
method.heading: Worked example: “It's less accurate than a quartz, isn't it?”
method.body:
A client is hesitating between a mechanical watch and a quartz watch. She says: “I've been told a mechanical watch is less accurate.” Here is an adviser's answer, using the three-step method.

**1. Listen.** “You want to be sure it will keep good time day to day, is that right?” *Rephrasing lets the client say what really worries her, and shows her she is heard.*

**2. Show.** The adviser turns the watch over: “See this little ring moving back and forth? That's the balance, the heart of the watch. It beats eight times a second, with no battery.” *Letting her see beats describing: the client watches the mechanism come alive.*

**3. Connect.** “You're right, a quartz is more accurate. What this one gives you is craftsmanship you can repair and pass on, without ever changing a battery. And day to day, a few seconds a day go unnoticed.” *Acknowledge first, then explain the value, then reframe around real use.*

The adviser neither denied the objection nor recited a spec sheet: he started from the client's question and led her to what matters to her.
objections.title: Three objections, three answers
objections.intro: Keep these answers in mind: they all follow the same method, listen, show, connect.
objection.quartz.title: “Less accurate than a quartz”
objection.quartz.body: **Acknowledge**: it's true, quartz is more accurate. **Explain**: the craftsmanship, no battery, a watch that can be repaired and passed on. **Reframe**: day to day, a few seconds a day are more than enough.
objection.stopped.title: “It stopped”
objection.stopped.body: **Reassure**: its power reserve has simply run out, it is not broken. **Explain**: an automatic winds itself when worn. **Advise**: wear it regularly, or wind it by hand before putting it back on.
objection.fragile.title: “It's fragile”
objection.fragile.body: **Reassure**: a shock-protection system protects the balance from everyday knocks. **Clarify**: water resistance is checked at every service. **Advise**: avoid falls and magnets, the watch's two real enemies.
objection.handover.title: Advice at handover
objection.handover.body: When you hand over the watch, three tips prevent most returns: **wind it** before wearing it for the first time, **don't change the date between 9 p.m. and 3 a.m.**, and plan **a service every five to seven years**.
s-evaluation.title: Assessment
quiz-functions.title: The functions
q-heart.prompt: On this diagram, which part measures time?
q-heart.alt: Diagram of a mechanical movement seen from the back, with five numbered markers placed on its parts.
q-heart.balance.fb: Its oscillations always last the same time: the balance and hairspring are what measure time.
q-heart.barrel.fb: The barrel supplies the energy, but its spring unwinds faster or slower: it cannot set a steady rhythm.
q-heart.escapement.fb: The escapement makes the tick-tock and releases the energy, but at the rhythm the balance imposes.
q-heart.train.fb: The gear train carries the energy; its wheels turn at the rhythm the escapement allows.
q-heart.hands.fb: The hands display time: they do not measure it.
q-frequency.prompt: On a product sheet, a client reads “28,800 vibrations per hour” and asks you what it means. What do you answer?
q-frequency.rhythm: It is the rhythm of the balance: 8 vibrations per second, or 4 hertz.
q-frequency.rhythm.fb: The frequency describes the balance's rhythm; 28,800 vibrations per hour means 8 per second, or 4 hertz.
q-frequency.reserve: It is the power reserve, expressed in seconds.
q-frequency.reserve.fb: The power reserve is expressed in hours (often 38 to 50): it is the spring's autonomy, not the balance's rhythm.
q-frequency.higher: The higher this figure, the better the watch, with no trade-off.
q-frequency.higher.fb: A higher frequency steadies the rate, but needs more energy and wears the parts more.
q-seconds.prompt: A client compares two watches and asks why the mechanical one's seconds hand seems to sweep while the quartz one's jumps. What do you explain?
q-seconds.steps: It moves in small steps, at the rhythm of the balance: 8 per second at 4 hertz.
q-seconds.steps.fb: At 4 hertz, the seconds hand makes 8 small steps a second, close enough together to look like a sweep.
q-seconds.continuous: The spring drives it continuously, without any jerk.
q-seconds.continuous.fb: The escapement releases the energy tooth by tooth: the hand moves in small steps, not continuously.
q-seconds.precise: Because a mechanical watch is more accurate than a quartz.
q-seconds.precise.fb: The smoothness of the seconds hand says nothing about precision; in fact, quartz is the more accurate.
quiz-situations.title: Situations
q-stopped.prompt: A client comes back from a long weekend. Her automatic watch, left on her bedside table, has stopped. What do you advise?
q-stopped.unwound: It has simply run down: wind it or wear it, then set the time again.
q-stopped.unwound.fb: Left off the wrist for several days, an automatic uses up its power reserve: it restarts as soon as it is wound or worn.
q-stopped.repair: Send it for repair: stopping means something is wrong.
q-stopped.repair.fb: Stopping after a few days off the wrist is normal behaviour, not a fault.
q-stopped.wait: Wait: an automatic winds itself, even when it's not worn.
q-stopped.wait.fb: An automatic winds itself through the movements of the wrist; left on a table, it does not wind.
q-magnetism.prompt: A client tells you his watch has been gaining 40 seconds a day since he started leaving it on his smart speaker every evening. What do you say?
q-magnetism.magnetism: It is probably magnetism; a watchmaker can demagnetise it.
q-magnetism.magnetism.fb: Speakers contain magnets; a magnetised hairspring makes the watch gain tens of seconds, and can be demagnetised in a few minutes.
q-magnetism.normal: That's normal: a mechanical watch always drifts that much.
q-magnetism.normal.fb: Normal drift is a few seconds a day; tens of seconds point to a problem.
q-magnetism.overwound: He has overwound his watch; the spring is damaged.
q-magnetism.overwound.fb: A slipping device stops the spring being wound beyond its limit: you cannot overwind a watch.
q-handover.prompt: You are handing over a mechanical watch to a client. Which advice do you give? Several answers are possible.
q-handover.wind: Wind it before wearing it for the first time.
q-handover.wind.fb: A spring wound from the start gives the watch its full power reserve.
q-handover.date: Avoid changing the date between 9 p.m. and 3 a.m.
q-handover.date.fb: On many movements, the date mechanism is engaged at those hours: changing it can damage it.
q-handover.service: Plan a service every five to seven years.
q-handover.service.fb: Oils age even when nothing is wrong; a service renews them and checks water resistance.
q-handover.only-broken: Only have it serviced if it breaks down.
q-handover.only-broken.fb: Waiting for a breakdown lets worn oils damage the parts: servicing is preventive.
q-handover.magnetic-case: Keep it in a case with a magnetic clasp, to protect it well.
q-handover.magnetic-case.fb: A magnetic clasp can magnetise the hairspring and make the watch gain.
quiz-explain.title: Explaining to the client
q-objection.prompt: A client tells you a mechanical watch is less accurate than a quartz. Which answer do you choose?
q-objection.acknowledge: “That's true. What it gives you is lasting craftsmanship, repairable, with no battery.”
q-objection.acknowledge.fb: This answer acknowledges an accurate fact, then highlights what gives a mechanical watch its value.
q-objection.deny: “Well regulated, a mechanical watch is just as accurate as a quartz, you know.”
q-objection.deny.fb: A mechanical watch drifts a few seconds a day, a quartz about 15 seconds a month: denying the gap loses the client's trust.
q-objection.dodge: “Look at this dial instead: the design makes all the difference.”
q-objection.dodge.fb: Changing the subject leaves the objection unanswered: the client keeps their doubt.
q-method-order.prompt: A client finds a mechanical watch “less accurate than a quartz”. Put the adviser's five actions in order.
q-method-order.rephrase: Rephrase their question to check what worries them
q-method-order.rephrase.fb: Listen first: rephrasing shows the client they are heard.
q-method-order.show: Turn the watch over and let them watch the balance
q-method-order.show.fb: Then show: seeing the mechanism come alive beats any description.
q-method-order.acknowledge: Acknowledge that quartz is more accurate
q-method-order.acknowledge.fb: Connecting starts by acknowledging an accurate fact, which makes the rest credible.
q-method-order.explain: Explain the craftsmanship, the absence of a battery and repairability
q-method-order.explain.fb: Then explain what gives a mechanical watch its value for them.
q-method-order.reframe: Reframe around daily use, where a few seconds a day are enough
q-method-order.reframe.fb: Finally, bring precision back to what it really means day to day.
q-jewels.prompt: “This one has more jewels, so it's better?” What do you answer?
q-jewels.construction: The number of jewels depends on the construction and functions: it is not, in itself, a sign of quality.
q-jewels.construction.fb: Jewels act as bearings; a watch with complications has more of them, without being better for it.
q-jewels.precision.fb: Jewels reduce friction and wear; they do not add precision in themselves.
q-jewels.decorative.fb: Jewels play a mechanical role: they are hard bearings that limit wear on the arbors.
recap.title: Key points
recap.heading: Remember before your next client
recap.p1: **Five functions, always in the same order**: energy (barrel), transmission (gear train), distribution (escapement), regulation (balance and hairspring) and display (hands).
recap.p2: **Behind every situation, a part**: stopped watch, power reserve run down; sudden gain, magnetism; upkeep, a service every five to seven years.
recap.p3: **Listen, show, connect**: acknowledge what is true, let them see the mechanism, then bring it back to what matters to the client.
recap.routine: **Your routine before answering**: which function are they talking about? What can I show them? What is the benefit for them? If you hesitate on any of these three questions, go back to the matching screen of this module.
